steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Beat eggs in a large bowl with an electric mixer until frothy.
Add sugar, butter, and flour; beat until smooth.
Stir in buttermilk, lemon juice, vanilla, and nutmeg.
Bake in the preheated oven until center is firm, 40 to 60 minutes.
Remove from the oven and cool for 1 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Buttermilk Pie
raw_recipe.description: This buttermilk pie is easy to whip up with buttermilk, eggs, butter, and sugar baked in a tender crust for a creamy and tangy old-fashioned dessert.

video.description: Soft, delicately sweet with a touch of tang from lemon juice and buttermilk, this old-fashioned custard pie is simply delectable. You’ll want to keep one on hand to impress guests.

review.reviewBody: I think, people should give review off of the recipe that is posted, not a recipe that they have created by changing what has been kindly given to us. Post your own, if you are just going to change everything, and then say I tweaked this, added that, and omitted this, other than that, was a great recipe. It frustrates me. This is a great pie, just the way it is, thank you for sharing.

My new favorite! I have made it twice. The first time the crust almost burned before inside done- so the second time I microwaved the inside in a glass bowl for 2minutes to speed up the cooking time inside. I also cooked the pie crust in the oven- I love my crust flakey on the bottom- After the pie crust was lightly cooked I poured the microwaved pie mixture in the pie and cooked till the crust was a nice brown and the inside was done. Awesome! I speed up many recipes using the microwave to precook the insides alittle faster. Pies or casseroles or baked potatoes!

This recipe will do but I have one that's been used in my family for generations that notes some differences: 3 eggs (beaten), 1 1/2 C. sugar, 1/2 cup (1 stick) butter (melted, cooled to lukewarm), 1/2 C. Buttermilk (make your own by adding a tabls. of vinegar to milk and let sit 1/2 hour - same chemical reaction), 2 Tabls. flour,rounded - not heaping, 1 teas. pure vanilla. Mix/sift together (sifting originated decades ago when flour almost always had mealy bugs in it!!) sugar and flour, add buttermilk, butter, eggs and vanilla. Mix well. Pour into pie shell (hard for the best cook to beat Pillsbury's frig crust - but use a Deep Dish if using frozen). Bake at 400 for 15 minutes. Reduce to 325 for apx. 30-40 minutes. Note: Pie should rise up in the middle - it will fall to level upon cooking. Additional test; shake - should not wiggle in the middle. This pie melts in your mouth and couldn't be easier. Variations: Add some fresh sliced peaches in a round across the top when in season. Or - Toss over some mini chocolate chips after that first 15 minutes. Enjoy whatever version!!

I had buttermilk that needed to be used. I used a frozen Pillsbury pie crust (blind baked before adding filling), lemon zest and vanilla but no lemon juice. Sprinkled nutmeg on top before putting in the oven. Lemon flavor was subtle, not overpowering. Perfect! Very good, and so easy! Will make again.

I made this without the crust, so I guess it wasn't really pie - but very different! And delicious!(That left out a lot of calories, too.) As long as I was juicing a lemon, I grated in about a tsp. or so of zest, which really "brightened" up the flavor. I loved it.
Update - 1/11/2018. This is just totally outstanding! I've been making it with the crust lately. So simple! As long as you have a bit of buttermilk, you can make it at 3PM & have a wonderful company-worthy dessert for dinner! I've been using Fiori di Sicilia extract from King Arthur Flour instead of the vanilla extract. (It's a combination of citrus oil and vanilla)The kitchen smells yummy for hours! And maybe closer to 2 teaspoons of finely chopped lemon zest. Or, maybe use lemon extract with the vanilla. Also, I've used a deep-dish clay pie baker. I can trim the raw crust to filling level, and place tin foil over the top, because my crust always over browns. The foil won't touch the custard, and mar the top when you take it off. Oh, you can cut the sugar back to about a cup.

I followed what a few others suggested - I used 1 cup of sugar and added 1 cup of coconut flakes. First time I used a regular ready made pie crust, it could not hold everything so the second time I used a deep dish crust and it was great!! Also, did not pre bake the crust so the crust didn't burn. Awesome awesome pie, especially when eaten cold. My husband couldn't stop himself!

I recommend: If you get frozen 9-inch pie crusts you MUST pre-cook it. Marie Callendar's pie crusts instruct people to pre-cook it about 10 mins at 400 degrees after pricking the sides and bottom thoroughly. First thaw them at room temp for 15 mins. This is very important. I think if people skip this step then any pies, specifically custard or pudding type pies will not set in the center. Secondly, I would use a Meyer lemon, these lemons are not so "sour" and they are great for cooking with a nice lemon but not sour flavor. A bit of lemon zest, as someone recommended, sure, why not? I cut the sugar down to only 1 C. Some people love super sweet pies and others do not. So it's personal taste. Just recall that true Southern pies tend to be very very sugary, so keep this in mind. Bon Appetit!

I really enjoyed this and so did the fam. Next time I'll use both lime and lemon juice and double it so it has more of a key lime flavor and skip the cinnamon. It was a little too sweet for me so next time I'll only use a cup of sugar. I did bake the crust for a few minutes before adding the mixture and I also microwave the pie mixture for four minutes prior to baking. I ended up baking two pies for about 65 minutes until they weren't giggly. Very good as written.

This was a pretty easy pie to make. I didn't have a deep dish pie crust so I used a normal one. I put the extra filling in a pie pan and baked it alongside the normal pie. It turned out nummy. I also didn't have nutmeg so I used pumpkin pie spice. It worked beautifully.

So easy and texture turned out great! Will cut sugar to one cup next time, but otherwise I wouldn’t change a thing. I used a glass Pyrex pie plate and Pillsbury refrigerated crust. Baked approximately 45 minutes. Will store in fridge after it cools.

I had never tasted buttermilk pie before, but wanted to use up some buttermilk before it went bad. I liked it and my husband who only likes chocolate, thought it was good. 

I don't like when people post about making a ton of changes, and I didn't make many. I went by other reviews and listened. I used a bit less lemon juice, added a shake of cinnamon. I did cook the pie crust a bit beforehand, covering the crust with aluminum foil so it wouldn't burn. I will make this again!
I made it without the crust. It is delicious and has a great texture. Next time I may use a crust but it is great without a crust.
Such an easy pie to make with basic ingredients. Sort of custard like
Some times I use rum flavor with/and or vanilla extract it's delicious

Very good overall. The butter needs to be VERY softened to incorporate fully - I had little pieces in the batter, but it baked up fine. I used premade crust and had a little extra filling that I cooked in a mini loaf pan. Used 1 tsp of lemon extract instead of juice. The bottom crust didn't bake enough. Definitely better after refrigeration, but eaten room temp. Will make again with slight adjustments (less sugar, more lemon extract, parbake crust or adjust cooking temp/time to hot 400 oven for 15ish minutes then dropping temp for remainder of the bake.) Pic: pie on right. Buttermilk cornbread, top L, butter swim biscuits bottom L.

I love this pie so much. No one in my family likes buttermilk pie bc they’re weird lol, but that’s great for me bc I love it so much and eat it all over several days. I would just add to make sure the butter is close to starting to melt so it won’t clump when it gets mixed with the cooler eggs. Otherwise, it’s a perfect easy recipe.
This is a good basic recipe. I used store bought pie crust and decreased sugar to 1 C. Next time, I'll try with more lemon juice and more nutmeg.
It was good, much better after refrigeration

Never heard of Buttermilk pie, but I had some leftover buttermilk, and thought I'd see what's out there. Found this recipe, made it as the recipe called for. Delicious! I have not made many pie crusts from scratch, so I tried this one. It turned out great! I will definitely make this again. I could see maybe some kind of fruit topping, We used whipped cream, which was spectacular!
So easy and delicious! Will definitely make this again!
